- Testing: Includes flammability, cold bend, cold impact, and additional ageing tests.

**Recommended Scheme: Scheme I - Standard Mark (ISI Mark Certification)**

Products conforming to IS 9873 (Part 1):2019 (Safety of Toys - Part 1: Safety Aspects Related to Mechanical and Physical Properties) are covered under a mandatory Quality Control Order (QCO) issued by the competent Central Ministry. Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or selling this product without a valid BIS license is prohibited under Section 16 of the BIS Act, 2016. Certification must be secured under Scheme I (Standard Mark / ISI Mark).

- Applicable Scheme: Scheme I - Standard Mark (ISI Mark License)
- Governing Standard: IS 9873 (Part 1):2019 (Safety of Toys - Part 1: Safety Aspects Related to Mechanical and Physical Properties)
- Statutory Order: S.O. 858(E) (Toys (Quality Control) Order, 2020)
- License Process: Requires complete factory quality control audit, verified in-house test infrastructure, and conforming laboratory test reports.
- Surveillance: Regular factory surveillance audits and random market sampling are mandated to maintain license validity.

**Recommended Scheme: Scheme II - Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS)**

Products covered under Electronics and IT Goods orders (such as IS 13252 (Part 1):2010 - Information Technology Equipment - Safety - Part 1: General Requirements) are governed by Scheme II (Compulsory Registration Scheme - CRS) under the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. Under CRS, manufacturers obtain registration through self-declaration of conformity based on laboratory test reports issued by BIS-recognized testing laboratories.

- Applicable Scheme: Scheme II - Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS)
- Governing Standard: IS 13252 (Part 1):2010 (Information Technology Equipment - Safety - Part 1: General Requirements)
- Notifying Authority & Order: Electronics and IT Goods Compulsory Registration Order 2012/2021
- Conformity Route: Self-declaration of conformity backed by mandatory product type testing at a BIS-recognized laboratory.
- Pre-grant Inspection: Pre-grant factory audit is not required under Scheme II; registration is granted on basis of valid test reports.

**Recommended Scheme: Scheme IV (Hallmarking of Precious Metals)**

Precious metals including gold jewellery and artefacts under IS 1417:2016 are governed by the statutory Hallmarking Scheme (Scheme IV) under Section 14 and 16 of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Certification is mandatory pursuant to the Gold and Gold Alloys Hallmarking Order, 2020. All articles must be certified and laser-marked with a 6-digit alphanumeric Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID).

- Applicable Scheme: Scheme IV - Hallmarking Scheme for Precious Metals
- Governing Standard: IS 1417:2016 (Gold and Gold Alloys, Jewellery/Artefacts - Fineness and Marking - Specification)
- Statutory Order: S.O. 4345(E) / Third Amendment 2026 (Mandatory)
- Marking Requirements: BIS Standard Logo, Purity in Karat and Fineness (e.g., 22K916), Assaying & Hallmarking Centre (AHC) mark, and 6-digit HUID
- Manufacturer Scope: Registered jewellers selling to domestic consumers; testing is performed via authorized AHC assay centers.

results.name: Foreign Cable Factory Scheme X FMCS
results.answer_preview: **Recommended Scheme: Scheme X - Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS)**  Overseas manufacturers exporting c
results.full_answer:
**Recommended Scheme: Scheme X - Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS)**

Overseas manufacturers exporting cables (governed by IS 694:2010: Polyvinyl Chloride Insulated Cables for Working Voltages Up to and Including 1100 V - Specification) to India must obtain certification under Scheme X (Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme - FMCS) pursuant to Section 13(1) of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. Under the mandatory Electrical Wires, Cables and Cords (Quality Control) Order, 2024 (Electrical Wires, Cables and Cords QCO 2024) issued by DPIIT, importing, selling, or distributing cables in India without a valid BIS Standard Mark (ISI) is strictly prohibited. Under Scheme X, BIS grants a license to use the Standard Mark following an on-site audit of overseas manufacturing facilities and independent sample testing in India.

- Applicable Scheme: Scheme X - Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS)
- Governing Standard: IS 694:2010 (Polyvinyl Chloride Insulated Cables for Working Voltages Up to and Including 1100 V - Specification)
- Statutory Order: Electrical Wires, Cables and Cords QCO 2024 / Electrical Wires, Cables and Cords QCO 2024 (Mandatory at Customs)
- Authorized Indian Representative (AIR): Foreign applicants must designate a resident Authorized Indian Representative responsible for statutory compliance and liaison with BIS.
- Verification Procedure: Satisfactory factory inspection by BIS auditor at the overseas plant, drawing of independent samples, and compliance verification in India.
- Marking Requirements: BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) with the overseas manufacturer's CM/L license number must be clearly printed on cables and reels.

results.name: Scheme I Domestic Plugs Roadmap
results.answer_preview: **Certification Process & Checklist: Scheme I (ISI Mark) for IS 1293 (Plugs and Socket-Outlets of Rated Voltage up to an
results.full_answer:
**Certification Process & Checklist: Scheme I (ISI Mark) for IS 1293 (Plugs and Socket-Outlets of Rated Voltage up to and Including 250 V and Rated Current up to and Including 16 A)**

To obtain Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) certification for IS 1293 (Plugs and Socket-Outlets of Rated Voltage up to and Including 250 V and Rated Current up to and Including 16 A) under Scheme I (Standard Mark), domestic manufacturers must complete a five-stage conformity assessment journey under the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. This procedure verifies factory quality management, test facility infrastructure, and product compliance against the Indian Standard.

**Step 1: Application & Documentation Submission**
   Prepare and submit the formal online application through the BIS Manakonline portal (Form-V under Scheme I). Pay the requisite application fee and upload verified corporate and technical documentation.
   - *Key Documentation*: Manufacturing facility layout and premises proof, List of manufacturing machinery and process flow chart, In-house testing equipment list with valid calibration certificates, Qualifications of designated Quality Control (QC) personnel, Trademark / brand authorization certificate
   - Ensure all in-house test equipment specified in the standard's Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT) is physically operational on site.

**Step 2: Factory Audit & Preliminary Inspection**
   A designated BIS Technical Officer conducts an on-site factory audit of the manufacturing unit. The auditor verifies production capability, quality control protocols, and competency of testing personnel.
   - *Key Documentation*: Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT) agreement, Raw material test certificates and vendor verification records, Calibration logs and maintenance registers
   - During the audit, the inspecting officer observes in-house testing of complete product parameters in accordance with the standard.

**Step 3: Sample Drawing & Laboratory Testing**
   The BIS inspecting officer draws independent random samples from the production line or finished goods storage. Samples are sealed and dispatched to authorized testing laboratories for complete type testing against IS 1293.
   - *Key Documentation*: Sample drawing counter-foil signed by the auditor and manufacturer, Independent laboratory test request dossier
   - Recognized Testing Facilities for IS 1293:
   -   * BIS Central Laboratory (CL) (Sahibabad, Uttar Pradesh) [Accreditation: NABL-TC-5001]
   -   * BIS Western Regional Laboratory (Mumbai, Maharashtra) [Accreditation: NABL-TC-5002]

**Step 4: Review of Test Reports & Grant of License (CML)**
   BIS technical scrutiny committees evaluate the factory inspection report and the independent test reports. Upon confirming complete conformity with all prescribed parameters, BIS issues the Certificate of Manufacturing License (CML).
   - *Key Documentation*: Grant of License Letter with unique 7-digit CML number, Official approval of the standard ISI Mark design and product packaging artwork
   - The licensee is assigned a unique CM/L (Certification Marks / License) number which must be displayed adjacent to the ISI monogram.

**Step 5: Surveillance, Quality Assurance & Renewal**
   Following the grant of license, the licensee must maintain regular production records and adhere to the SIT. BIS conducts periodic unannounced surveillance audits and draws market samples to ensure ongoing quality compliance.
   - *Key Documentation*: Annual license renewal application (Form-VI), Periodic production and marking returns, Marking fee calculation statement
   - Licenses are initially granted for 1 to 2 years and are renewable upon payment of marking fees and verification of consistent quality history.

Sources: [EV1]

results.full_answer:
**Status: Verification Required (Unconfirmed Currentness)**

IS 1417 specifies the hallmarking requirements for gold jewellery, focusing on fineness and marking specifications. The standard outlines procedures for handling test items, permissible sizes for hallmarks, and the necessary security measures for the storage of jewellery during the hallmarking process.

- **Handling of Test Items:**
  - Hallmarked gold jewellery is accepted for fineness verification (Clause 5.4.1).
  - Individual items must be segregated into lots (Clause 5.4.2).
  - A unique code number is assigned for tracking throughout processing (Clause 5.4.3).
  - The hallmarking process should be completed within 48 hours (Clause 5.4.7).

- **Permissible Sizes of Hallmarks:**
  - Height of hallmark for gold articles:
    - 1.5 mm, 1.0 mm, 0.75 mm, 0.50 mm (Clause 5.9.3.3).
    - For articles below 2 grams, a marking size of 0.3 mm is permitted.

results.full_answer:
**स्थिति: सत्यापन आवश्यक (असत्यापित वर्तमानता)**

प्राप्त दस्तावेज़ों से संकेत मिलता है कि ISI चिह्न को प्रत्येक प्लग या सॉकेट-आउटलेट और इसके पैकेजिंग पर शामिल किया जाना चाहिए, बशर्ते कि उत्पाद संबंधित विनिर्देशों के अनुरूप हो। हालाँकि, यह स्पष्ट रूप से नहीं कहा गया है कि क्या ISI चिह्न सभी घरेलू प्लग और सॉकेट के लिए अनिवार्य है। ISI चिह्न के संबंध में वर्तमान आवश्यकताओं की पुष्टि के लिए आधिकारिक भारतीय मानकों या सक्षम प्राधिकरणों के खिलाफ सत्यापन की आवश्यकता है।

- ISI चिह्न को प्रत्येक प्लग या सॉकेट-आउटलेट और इसके पैकेजिंग पर स्पष्ट और स्थायी रूप से अंकित किया जाना चाहिए।
- अंकन उत्पाद के संबंधित विनिर्देशों के अनुरूप होने पर निर्भर करता है।
- अतिरिक्त अंकन आवश्यकताओं में पैकेजिंग पर BIS प्रमाणन विवरण का संदर्भ शामिल है।

उपभोक्ता आधिकारिक BIS Care मोबाइल ऐप का उपयोग करके ISI चिह्न की प्रामाणिकता या लाइसेंस की वैधता की पुष्टि कर सकते हैं।
